questions.q: What core problem does Data Cloud (Data 360) address?
options: Dashboards that take too long to render
Customer data scattered across systems with no shared identity
The lack of a query language in Salesforce
Sandboxes that cannot be refreshed
questions.explain: Customer data lives in many systems with different IDs and field names. Data Cloud ingests, harmonizes, and unifies it so one profile can be analyzed or activated.

questions.q: In the Ana Ruiz example, why is the customer count inflated?
options: Because dashboards double every number
Because the CRM duplicates every record on export
Because web forms are always counted twice
Each system sees a different person, and nothing links the three records
questions.explain: Without a shared key or identity matching, each system's record counts as a separate customer, which inflates totals and blocks cross-system questions.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of the four jobs described in this lesson?
options: Unify, ingest, act, harmonize
Act, ingest, unify, harmonize
Ingest, harmonize, unify, then analyze and act
Harmonize, act, ingest, unify
questions.explain: Data streams ingest, mapping harmonizes into a common model, identity resolution unifies records, and insights and segments support analysis and action.

questions.q: Which job decides that records under different emails are the same person?
options: Identity resolution (unify)
Ingestion
Segmentation
Dashboard faceting
questions.explain: Identity resolution matches records that describe the same individual and links them into a unified profile.

questions.q: How should you treat Data Cloud feature names and limits you read about?
options: As permanent, since Salesforce never renames products
As irrelevant to analysts
As always identical across editions and orgs
As things to verify in current release notes, since names and features change
questions.explain: The platform has been renamed (now Data 360 as of this writing) and its features, licensing, and connectors change by release.
